Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

cellpaintr 0.1.0

  • Experimental version still under development

cellpaintr 0.2.0

  • Version used internally in our lab

cellpaintr 0.3.0

  • Getting it ready for submission to Bioconductor

cellpaintr 0.99.0

  • Submitted to Bioconductor

cellpaintr 0.99.4

  • calculateStats() calibrates the t-statistic with a permutation test that relabels whole patients and refits all leave-one-out models (method = "permutation", the new default). It enumerates all relabelings if there are at most n_permutations + 1 of them and samples them otherwise. method = "t" keeps the p-values from the t-distribution, which are anti-conservative because the scores of different held-out patients are correlated.
  • predictLOO() records its settings in metadata(), and calculateStats() takes the interest and reference levels from there instead of from the order of the factor levels.
  • volcanoPlot() accepts precomputed statistics (stats) and passes further arguments, such as method, to calculateStats().

cellpaintr 0.99.5

  • The permutation test of calculateStats() handles mixed designs, in which only some patients have cells of both levels, for example after quality control removed all cells of one level of a patient. It swaps the levels of the patients with both levels, permutes the levels among the other patients, and reports which patients have cells of one level only.

cellpaintr 0.99.6

  • calculateStats() offers a corrected paired t-test (method = "corrected"). For every pair of patients, it refits the models without both of them and adds the products of their influences on each other’s score differences to the sample variance, which makes the variance unbiased under the null hypothesis. It needs n(n-1)/2 fits per feature group for n patients instead of refitting all models for every relabeling, and it can reach small p-values with few patients. The attribute variance_ratio holds the corrected over the uncorrected variance. The permutation test stays the default.
  • Internal: model fitting of compute_y_hat() moved into helpers shared with the corrected t-test; results are unchanged.

cellpaintr 0.99.7

Changes in response to the first Bioconductor review:

  • generate_data() is renamed generateData(), in line with the rest of the API.
  • New example data: inst/extdata/jump_subset.csv.gz, 240 cells of the JUMP Cell Painting dataset (DMSO, AMG900, and dexamethasone on four plates) as exported by CellProfiler; inst/scripts/make-jump-subset.R documents how it was made, and inst/scripts/README.md the provenance of all files in inst/extdata.
  • The vignette is rewritten around the JUMP data: it describes the CellProfiler input and its Metadata_ columns, explains every step, and shows the messages of calculateStats().
  • New package man page (?cellpaintr) with an overview of the workflow.
  • Exported functions validate their inputs and stop with informative messages; predictLOO() accepts a character target, needs at least two levels of group, and keeps the cell names of sce instead of replacing them with integers.
  • loadData() passes further arguments to readr::read_csv(), for example num_threads.
  • removeNAs(), removeLowVariance(), removeZeroInflation(), and transformScale() have an assay_type argument, and use vectorized colSums(), rowMeans(), and MatrixGenerics instead of apply().
  • The relabelings of the permutation test run through future.apply::future_lapply(), sequentially by default and in parallel after future::plan(), with reproducible random numbers.
  • Functions are imported instead of declared as global variables; rlang, stats, methods, MatrixGenerics, and future.apply are imported.
  • Long functions are split into helpers, and the code follows the Bioconductor style (80 characters, 4-space indents).
  • compute_y_hat() and aggregateYhat() are internal and have no man pages.
  • More unit tests check values, not only classes, and cover the input checks.

Changes to improve the package but unrelated to the Bioconductor review:

  • The corrected t-test of calculateStats() (method = "corrected") now divides the paired t-statistic by sqrt(2(n-1)/(n-2)), the factor by which it is too large if each score difference is a sum of pairwise interactions with the other patients. It needs no refits and no longer needs the settings of predictLOO(). It replaces the leave-two-out variance correction of 0.99.6 and its attribute variance_ratio.
  • calculateStats() offers the correction of the corrected resampled t-test of Nadeau and Bengio (2003) (method = "nadeau_bengio"), which divides the paired t-statistic by sqrt((2n-1)/(n-1)). It corrects less than method = "corrected" and needs a paired design with at least two patients and no refits.
  • The permutation test of calculateStats() no longer refits relabelings that only repeat another one. Exchanging the two levels in all patients at once turns every score into one minus the score and leaves the statistic unchanged, so one patient now keeps its labels whenever this exchange is itself a relabeling (always in a paired design). This halves the number of refits, and the test stays exact. In a paired design with n patients, there are 2^(n-1) relabelings, and the smallest attainable p-value is 2^(1-n) instead of a nominal 2^-n that depended on the forest seeds.
  • The vignette explains that ROC curves and AUCs use the mean scores of each replicate and condition.
  • The vignette scales the well means before the PCA. Robust z-scores are extreme for features with a median absolute deviation close to zero, and one well dominated the first principal component.

Bug fixes:

  • plotROC() and plotAUC() take the interest and reference levels from the settings of predictLOO() instead of from the order of the factor levels of target. Before, a character target whose interest level sorted first alphabetically, such as AMG900 against DMSO, swapped the two levels and turned every AUC into one minus the AUC.
  • predictLOO() orders the levels of a character target with the reference level first.
